concerns: Run 3 beats run 1 by 0.0576 PR-AUC, which is under one SD (about 0.06), so the gain is not clearly real. Run 3 beats run 2 by only 0.0345, well within one SD.

The simplicity rule favors logistic (run 1) unless a complex model wins by more than 1 SD. No complex model clears that bar against run 1 (the largest gap, 0.0576, is just under SD 0.0595-0.0617). Run 2 is not simpler than logistic, so it is carried forward only as a hedge; treat the logistic baseline as the fallback if no later run is clearly better.

The PotentialFraud label has an undocumented origin and may reflect a prior audit rule or a rule-derived flag, so the high ROC-AUC (about 0.94) and PR-AUC (about 0.7) may reflect label leakage or proxy features rather than real fraud detection. Even a plain logistic model on 50 features reaches 0.94, which is suspicious.
Size features (volume and counts) may act as proxies for the labeling mechanism; the no_size ablation was run only for logistic and LightGBM with confounded settings.

Agent features are 19 aggregate ratios, and their effect is confounded with the imbalance setting and the model in runs 3 and 4. Run 4 differs from run 3 in several ways at once, so no single factor can be isolated.
Fold SD of about 0.06-0.076 is large with only about 506 positives, so the ranking among runs is noisy. Precision@50 differences of 0.02-0.06 amount to 1-3 providers.
The queue is about 100 providers but only precision@50 is reported, so precision at the real queue size is unknown. Claims cover one year, so temporal generalization is untested.

next_experiments.rationale: Isolates the agent-feature effect in the simplest model, to test whether the gain comes from the features or from LightGBM.
A more regularized version of run 3, to check whether its edge holds with less capacity and under the noise.
A strongly regularized, simple baseline with size included, to test the size-proxy and leakage concern.

concerns: Best PR-AUC is 0.7389 (run 6) vs 0.7068 for logistic run 7; the gap is 0.032, smaller than the fold SD of about 0.056-0.065, so the complex models do not clear the one-SD bar and the simpler logistic is preferred.
Run 3 and run 6 are essentially tied at 0.7385 and 0.7389, which suggests a plateau across LightGBM settings rather than a real signal.
Fold SD of about 0.06 on 5,410 providers (about 506 positives) means differences between runs of 0.03 are within noise; ranking of configs is unreliable.

ROC-AUC of 0.94-0.95 and PR-AUC around 0.7 at 9.35% prevalence is high for a label of unknown origin; the label may be rule-derived or partly leaked via features such as size, money or duplication, so the model may reproduce the labelling rule rather than find fraud.

Agent features add only modest gains (logistic no_size 0.6809 to 0.6872, within noise) and their construction (aggregated per provider, with possible target-adjacent info) should be checked for leakage.
Precision at 50 is 0.74-0.80 but the queue holds about 100; precision at 100 was not reported and may be lower.
Folds are not described as time-aware or grouped; with claims from a single year, provider-level or temporal leakage across folds is possible.
Imbalance handling (class_weight, none) shows no consistent benefit, so no reason to add complexity such as SMOTE.

review.split_comment: Stratified provider-level 5-fold CV keeps each provider in a single fold and preserves the 9.35% flagged rate, which is suitable for PR-AUC. Features are per-provider aggregates, so there is no cross-fold leakage apart from the unclear scope of dup_any_provider. A time-based check would be a useful supplement, since claims span only about one year, and the undocumented label origin means results measure agreement with suspicion flags rather than confirmed fraud.

1.rationale: Regularized linear baseline without size features to test whether signal comes from behavior rather than provider volume; cheap and stable reference.

2.rationale: Bagged trees with leaf smoothing on all features capture nonlinear interactions and are robust to noisy suspicion labels; class weighting helps top-of-ranking precision.

3.rationale: Moderate-capacity gradient boosting with agent features added to test whether extra aggregated signals improve PR-AUC; no resampling to keep probabilities well ranked.

4.rationale: Low-capacity, heavily regularized boosting without size features but with agent features to check robustness and reduce reliance on volume proxies and overfitting to uncertain labels.

5.rationale: Isolates the agent-feature effect in the simplest model, to test whether the gain comes from the features or from LightGBM.

6.rationale: A more regularized version of run 3, to check whether its edge holds with less capacity and under the noise.

7.rationale: A strongly regularized, simple baseline with size included, to test the size-proxy and leakage concern.
